efficacy.note: LuCaP PDX-derived organoids tested for olaparib sensitivity by BRCA2 genotype; prediction is which genotype responds.
efficacy.short: LuCaP organoids: olaparib by BRCA2 genotype
efficacy.quote: The utility of the platform as a genotype-dependent model of drug sensitivity was tested with olaparib and carboplatin.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6125202). model_kind ex_vivo: patient-derived tumour passaged as PDX and assayed as organoids in vitro; the enum has no PDX-organoid value.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the comparison is in the same paper and is scored as the next entry. The paper was written knowing TOPARP-A; the retrodiction flag sits on the retro entry, not the opener (lint).
efficacy.population: LuCaP PDX-derived organoid lines of three BRCA2 genotypes: wild-type, single-copy loss (LuCaP 86.2), two-copy loss (LuCaP 86.2CR)

efficacy.model: LuCaP PDX-derived organoid platform: olaparib dose-response across BRCA2 wild-type, single-copy-loss (LuCaP 86.2) and two-copy-loss (LuCaP 86.2CR) mCRPC organoids (Beshiri 2018)
efficacy.note: BRCA2 two-copy-loss LuCaP 86.2CR organoids >100-fold more olaparib-sensitive than hemizygous or wild-type lines; paper pairs this with TOPARP-A BRCA2 responders.
efficacy.quote: Finally, we observed maximum cytotoxicity to the PARP inhibitor olaparib in BRCA2-/- organoids, similar to responses observed in patients.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. The patient side is TOPARP-A's published genotype-level result, not the organoid donors' own outcomes; the LuCaP 86.2/86.2CR donor was never treated with olaparib. Only olaparib tested; IC50 0.48 uM (86.2CR) vs 65.0 uM (86.2).
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction under decision 10: the experiment is framed 'To compare organoids to genotype-determined patient responses' citing TOPARP-A (2015), so the match is retro, never same. Patient-level track: the prediction is which BRCA2 genotype responds. magnitude direction_only because organoid IC50 and patient time to progression are different quantities.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: Organoid olaparib IC50 by BRCA2 genotype (0.48 vs 65.0 uM, >100-fold) against TOPARP-A response by BRCA2 status: different quantities, direction only
efficacy.population: LuCaP 86.2 (BRCA2 hemizygous), LuCaP 86.2CR (BRCA2 two-copy loss) and BRCA2-wild-type LuCaP organoids vs TOPARP-A BRCA2-loss mCRPC patients (Mateo 2015)

patient_trials.quote: Treatment with the PARP inhibitor olaparib in patients whose prostate cancers were no longer responding to standard treatments and who had defects in DNA-repair genes led to a high response rate.

dose.note: Sponsor Simcyp PBPK model built to predict olaparib exposure with CYP3A inhibitors and inducers; FDA asked for it to set DDI dose modifications.
dose.quote: A PBPK model of olaparib was developed by the sponsor to predict the effect of strong CYP3A inhibitor itraconazole or inducer rifampin on the exposure of olaparib
dose.confidence_note: Bundle text of the 2014 clinical pharmacology review, Appendix 3.3 (PBPK review). An in-silico clinical-pharmacology model, not an efficacy model; its own track because it is a different system with a different prediction (exposure under CYP3A modulation).
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first regulatory use (2014 capsule NDA 206162, ovarian). The model was verified against DDI studies already run; the retrodiction flag sits on the retro entry, not the opener (lint).
dose.population: Simcyp olaparib PBPK model; capsule 400 mg BID; simulations for itraconazole, rifampin, fluconazole and efavirenz

dose.model: Olaparib Simcyp PBPK model (sponsor-built, FDA-reviewed) predicting olaparib exposure with CYP3A inhibitors and inducers; set the DDI dose modifications on the Lynparza label (NDA 206162 2014; Model 6, NDA 208558 2017)
dose.note: PBPK reproduced the itraconazole AUC ratio (2.75 vs 2.66 observed) but under-predicted rifampin (0.32 vs 0.12); FDA still used it for moderate-modulator dose rules.
dose.quote: As shown in Table 2, PBPK reasonably predicted mean AUC ratio and Cmax ratio by itraconazole. However, the observed and PBPK predicted AUC ratio by inducer rifampin were 0.12 and 0.32, respectively (Table 3).
dose.confidence_note: Comparison made in the capsule-era DDI studies (advanced solid tumours, not prostate; the quoted passage does not name the study populations). Cross-indication PK admitted under the healthy-volunteer PK rule; the same DDI dose modifications carry on the 2020 mCRPC label. The dose rule's 'enough' half is untested: efficacy at DDI-reduced doses was never trialled.
dose.reason: Reproduced observed CYP3A DDI, inducer under-predicted
dose.judgement: Retro under decision 10: FDA 'verified' the model against clinical DDI studies already run, so it reproduces rather than predicts. Itraconazole within 2x, rifampin off 2.7x in the right direction, and FDA answered 'Yes' on adequacy: partial. The fluconazole and efavirenz predictions that set the moderate-modulator doses were never tested in patients, so no prospective entry follows.
dose.magnitude_basis: PBPK-predicted vs observed olaparib AUC ratio: itraconazole 2.75 vs 2.66, rifampin 0.32 vs 0.12 (2.7-fold)
dose.population: Olaparib capsule DDI studies with itraconazole and rifampin vs Simcyp PBPK simulations; ovarian-cancer NDA 206162, DDI dose rules carried to the mCRPC label

considered_not_added: Karkampouna 2021 Nat Commun PNPCa PDX/organoids (PMC7892572): the model carries a BRCA2 mutation but has no PARP-inhibitor arm; olaparib appears only in the discussion and a reference, so no comparison exists.

Elsesy 2023 Mol Oncol CRPC tumour-slice cultures and patient-derived organoids (PMID 36694344): olaparib sensitivity via RAD51 loss, but no donor-level clinical olaparib outcome to compare; its class-level claim (castration-induced BRCAness explains the PROpel HRR-wild-type benefit) is the ar-parp-crosstalk-xenografts prediction on another model and postdates PROpel/MAGNITUDE, so it adds no track.
FDA ODAC 2023-04-28 (sNDA 208558/S-025, PROpel) and the 2023 BRCAm-only Lynparza label: a patient-side tier-2 source for the existing ar-parp-crosstalk-xenografts track, not a model system.
EMA Lynparza II/0036 EPAR (2020, BRCA1/2-only indication): patient-side tier-2 dating for the existing hrr-gene-panel-cell-screen and atm-null-prostate-isogenic tracks, not a model system.
Niraparib dog DAT binding / blood-pressure secondary pharmacology (Zejula 2017 review) vs MAGNITUDE hypertension: an unscored entry on the existing parpi-rat-dog-toxicology track, not a new system.
Janssen 2022-02-15 (MAGNITUDE Cohort 2 futility) and AstraZeneca 2021-09-24 (PROpel) press releases: tier-5 dating for existing tracks only.

Fuzuloparib (member): prostate patient data exist (phase 1b with AAP, BMC Cancer 2026 PMC13560133; FAST-PC neoadjuvant with abiraterone, Cell Rep Med 2025 PMID 40056906; FUZUPRO NCT04691804 interim ASCO 2026 abstract only), but no fuzuloparib-specific prostate model was found; its preclinical basis (BRCA-mutant xenografts; AR-PARP combination) is the same system as the brca2-null-synthetic-lethality and ar-parp-crosstalk-xenografts tracks, so these are patient-side entries for existing tracks.

Talazoparib popPK/PD (NDA 217439, 2023): formulation-bridging simulations (Cmax +37-52% with no haematology effect), no dose prediction compared with patients; the 0.5 mg dose with enzalutamide came from observed P-gp DDI data.
Niraparib/abiraterone population PK and exposure-response (NDA 216793, 2023): descriptive of MAGNITUDE data with no prior prediction to compare.

Talazoparib (Shen 2013 MX-1/Capan-1), niraparib (Jones 2009 MDA-MB-436) and fuzuloparib BRCA-mutant xenografts: same synthetic-lethality system and prediction as the brca2-null-synthetic-lethality track; not widened into separate tracks.

MURAL PDX collection (Risbridger 2021) and the 2025-2026 PDO drug-screening platforms surfaced by search: no PARP-inhibitor arm with a patient comparison identified at abstract level; not pursued within budget.
